description: HMAC-SHA256 signing of a context carrying SUB-SECOND timestamps -- all languages must produce identical signatures
notes: Regression fixture for spec section 2 rule 5. The input timestamps carry MICROSECOND precision (.123456Z / .987654Z) but the canonical form truncates them to MILLISECONDS (.123Z / .987Z). This case exists because the whole-second fixture cannot detect a precision mismatch: Python and .NET natively serialize microseconds while JavaScript's Date cannot represent them at all, so without a mandated precision the same instant signed in different languages produced different bytes and failed to verify cross-SDK. Truncation (not rounding) is required so an expiry is never moved later than the issuer intended.
